arguments.heading: What happened at the argument
paragraphs: Sarah Schrup argued moral capacity defines criminal culpability.
She stated this understanding persists in most jurisdictions.
Elizabeth Prelogar argued the side that brought the case failed to prove a constitutional violation.
She stated the state legislature made a valid policy choice.

sections.heading: What this case is about
paragraphs: Kansas law requires defendants to know an act is illegal to claim insanity. It does not require proof that the defendant understood the act was morally wrong. the side that brought the case argues this standard violates the Constitution. The state argues it has the right to define criminal culpability.

sections.heading: Why it matters
paragraphs: This case defines the constitutional limits on state insanity defenses. It determines whether moral judgment is a required element of criminal responsibility. The outcome shapes how states evaluate defendant culpability in criminal trials.
